title: Audit Snapshot Chronology & Delegated Access Explorer - Prototype and Review
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Admins and auditors struggle to rapidly answer time-bound questions about who had which permissions, why a change was made, and which resources were affected. Existing audit views are flat event lists; they do not surface effective permissions over time or enable quick remediation paths.

Goal: Design a compact, scannable Console UX that lets enterprise admins and compliance teams: (1) 'time-travel' to audit snapshots (view effective roles/permissions at a historical timestamp), (2) quickly understand the chronology of role/permission changes with causal context, and (3) explore delegated access (who can act as whom) and run bulk-remediation or approval flows. Deliver high-fidelity prototypes, user-research notes, and developer-facing specs for implementation.

Scope: The work covers the Audit page and Workspace Settings > Access sections: chronology strip, snapshot panel (read-only historical view), delegated access explorer modal, event detail flyout, and a light-weight remediation action sheet (request approval / initiate role rollback). Does NOT include backend audit storage/schema changes — those are handled in ENG-3194.

Constraints: Must work within existing Console navigation and theming, align with Console accessibility patterns, and avoid performance-heavy client-side data transforms (will rely on server-side endpoints in ENG-3194/3220). Prototypes should assume paginated event streams and precomputed snapshots returned by the API.
acceptance_criteria: Chronology strip shows a condensed timeline of role/permission events with zoomable ranges and hover tooltips
Snapshot panel displays effective roles, resource-scoped permissions, and bindings for a selected timestamp with visual diffs compared to the current state
Delegated Access Explorer allows admins to input a principal and see a graph-style path of delegation (who granted access, when, and via which role), with export/CSV option
Event detail flyout surfaces change rationale (if present), associated PR/issue links, and a one-click remediation menu (request approval, revoke, or schedule rollback)
Prototypes pass lightweight usability testing with 6 enterprise admin participants (task completion >= 80% and SUS >= 70) and documented feedback
Design handoff includes component-level tokens, interaction notes, and a prioritized implementation backlog for ENG
comments: 2026-02-17 - Maya Chen: Initial wireframes uploaded to Figma. Focused on three core tasks: answer 'who had access on X', 'why was a role assigned', and 'roll back an accidental grant'.
2026-02-23 - Liam O'Connor: Reviewed early flows with PM and Eng; noted backend needs for snapshot diffs (ENG-3194) and delegation graph API (ENG-3220). Added dependencies.
2026-03-02 - PM (Harpreet Singh): Requested explicit export/CSV for compliance reporting and an audit retention banner. Confirmed high customer impact and compliance priority.
2026-03-05 - Design critique: Accessibility concern flagged for timeline keyboard navigation; propose alternate 'list mode' for screen readers. Liam to prototype keyboard-first controls.

2026-03-08 - Maya Chen: Usability testing (6 participants) completed — users completed primary tasks; main friction was locating the remediation actions. Proposal: introduce persistent action affordance in snapshot header.
2026-03-10 - Liam O'Connor: Updated prototype with persistent action affordance, added visual diff bar, and included quick links to related PRs/Issues. Ready for ENG handoff and design QA.
key_decisions: Use server-provided 'snapshot' payloads to avoid client heavy lifting; UI will render diffs locally based on snapshot vs current state
Timeline will default to condensed mode with zoom controls; provide 'list mode' for screen reader accessibility
Delegated Access Explorer will present a linear graph with optional adjacency table export rather than free-form force-directed graph (simpler for compliance export and implementation)
Remediation actions are gated by a confirmation + optional approval workflow if RBAC policy requires it (ties into PM-4820 approval engine)
risks: Backend snapshot APIs may be slower than expected — will require UX fallbacks (skeletons + progressive reveal)
Complex delegation graphs for large orgs may overwhelm the UI — mitigation: sampling and 'expand on demand' with export for full graphs
Approval/remediation flows intersect with security controls — must coordinate security sign-off prior to release
accessibility_notes: Timeline controls must be fully keyboard operable and provide ARIA live regions for time-travel changes. Provide an alternate 'list mode' that exposes the same information in a screen-reader friendly linear layout. Color diffs use WCAG-compliant palettes with redundant patterns for colorblind users.
